newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's UNITA sends first deputies to capital.
newsitem.headline: Angola's UNITA sends first deputies to capital.

text.p: Angola's former rebel UNITA movement on Wednesday sent 12 of its 70 deputies to the government-held capital Luanda to take their places in a unity administration with the MPLA after two decades of civil war.
It also sent three out of a total of four ministers who will head the ministries of tourism, commerce and health in the first peace-time government.

The ruling MPLA and UNITA fought a 19-year civil war until 1994 when they signed a peace accord to end the fighting which erupted soon after independence from Portugal in 1975. The pact agreed to merge both their armies and establish a united government.
The UNITA delegates were flown by the United Nations, overseeing the implementation of the peace plan, from UNITA's central highlands stronghold of Bailundo to Luanda.
"I am satisfied that they are here in as far as this is a symbol of UNITA's commitment to peace," U.N. special envoy to Angola Alioune Blondin Beye said at the airport.
"But I would have liked to have seen all of them. I am sure though that they have brought important information that will be helpful to the peace process," Beye said.

UNITA captured 70 seats in parliament during elections in 1992 won by President Jose Eduardo dos Santos' MPLA. The biref peace collapsed when UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi rejected the outcome of the poll and returned to war.
Among the UNITA ministers that arrived was Victorino Hossi, set to become Angola's commerce minister, Anastacio Sikato, health minister and Jorge Valentim, tourism minister.
UNITA failed to send Kayaya Kahala, its choice to head the ministry of geology and mines -- a key department in diamond-rich Angola.

An official close to the peace process told Reuters Kahala had not arrived because he was involved in negotiations with the government on the carving up of the diamond areas controlled mainly by the former rebels.
UNITA rakes in about $300 million to $600 million from diamonds annually and the government earns about $200 million from diamond revenue.
The government's peace negotiator Higino Carneiro was among officials to greet the UNITA members on their arrival.
"You are welcome to Luanda," Carneiro told them. "We would like to have seen all of you but at least this is a start," he added.

UNITA's chief negotiator in a joint ceasfire commission, Isaias Samakuva said: "This is a vanguard group, now the government needs to show flexibility. Now I hope the government will respond to this gesture."

UNITA has said it will not go through with a unity government until the MPLA unveils a programme for national reconciliation. It also has insisted on further talks on the future role of Savimbi in a unity government.
